hyps.why: Without the direct 0->3 edge, removing edge 5 leaves only edge 4 feeding the output, severely bottlenecking the cell.
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 5 leaves the output fed only by the shallow direct edge, collapsing depth.
If edge 5 is none, removing edge 3 leaves only edge 4 reaching the output, drastically reducing capacity.
When edge 1 is none, node 2 depends entirely on node 1, so cutting edge 0 kills all intermediate computation.
If node 2 does not connect to the output, a conv on edge 2 contributes nothing.
A conv into node 2 is wasted when node 2 has no path to the output.
With edge 0 none, node 1 is empty, so a conv on edge 4 only processes zeros.
A conv reading from node 1 is useless when node 1 receives no input.
Replacing weak parameter-free pooling with a 3x3 conv gives a larger gain than replacing other ops.
Pooling just before the output hurts, so swapping it for a 3x3 conv yields an outsized improvement.
